resources.string: ClipHistory needs a free helper app to see what you copy. Shizuku-Next is the recommended option for the best compatibility, and it starts by itself after every restart. Tap Download, then open the downloaded file and install it. If your phone asks, allow installing apps from your browser. Already use Shizuku or another compatible app? That works too, and you can skip this step. To switch to Shizuku-Next, uninstall Shizuku first: the two can’t be installed side by side.
Connect to Wi-Fi. Tap About phone below, then tap Build number 7 times. Enter your PIN if asked. This unlocks Developer options.
Tap Developer options below. Find Wireless debugging, turn it on and choose Always allow on this network.
Open Shizuku-Next and tap Start. The first time, it asks you to pair once: in Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code, then type the 6-digit code into Shizuku-Next’s notification.

Come back here, tap Connect and choose Always allow. Copy any text to check: it appears at the top of your history. Pause recording before copying private text that another app might not mark sensitive.
All set. ClipHistory is connected and saves what you copy.
Install a browser to open this link.
Saved text could not be read. Check Diagnostics and try again.
Recording is available, but some earlier clipboard events were dropped during overload. Those copies cannot be recovered.
